videos.caption: We had many people in our comments who assumed we were just random people who bought a tiger cub and many people asking where they can get a tiger. We want to address this because it’s very important. Rick is not just a normal person with a tiger. Rick owns a USDA licensed zoo and Mowgli is not a personal pet. Mowgli came from another zoo and was not purchased as a pet. The reason Mowgli is inside the house (which is on the zoo property) is because he is not fully vaccinated and we will not allow him outside until our vet clears us for that. Anyone who is wanting a pet tiger needs to know that you cannot legally own one as a pet. Also, this is not Rick’s first Tiger. You can go and see Kai, our female, on our page. Rick has extensive experience with big cats and raising them. You can however enjoy how cute he is on our social media! We will NEVER have tiger encounters available and no visitors will ever be allowed to touch him or interact with him. When he is older and cleared to go outside you can see him in his enclosure if you visit the zoo. We hope that clears a few things up!

A baby tiger’s roar is more of a high-pitched squeak or mewl than the deep, commanding roar of an adult. These vocalisations help tiger cubs communicate with their mother and siblings, often signaling hunger, playfulness, or seeking attention. While not as powerful as an adult’s roar, these sounds are an adorable glimpse into the cub’s journey of learning and growing into a formidable predator. Hoy en noticias de México: lamentablemente la historia de Pepe el Tigre de Cancún tiene más aristas: hoy nos da pena por identificarnos con un abuelito vulnerable que cuida a su mascota, pero en realidad el señor lucraba con sus tigres de bengala, pantera, jaguares, exhibiéndolos en un show para su restaurante a precios costosos dirigidos A Turistas extranjeros, famosos y políticos. Durante mucho tiempo hizo millones con su negocio, pero el huracán destruyó su restaurante en 2005. En los siguientes seis años mantuvo a sus animales pero sin darles vida digna, por lo que en 2011 se los incautaron según las nuevas leyes de bienestar animal. La verdad es que sus tigres jamás desaparecieron, sino que fueron enviados a diferentes zoológicos y santuarios (con información confirmada por organizaciones ambientales). Tampoco existió el llamado santuario de Pepe: en sus propios videos pueden comprobar que en realidad operaba como un terreno con jaulas para resguardar a sus felinos. Grumpy Kallie is waiting for breakfast. 😊 Today, on International Tiger Day, we’re honored to introduce you to Kallie—a tiger whose survival is nothing short of a miracle. When Kallie was rescued by Lions Tigers & Bears, she had been abandoned and left to die. Her condition was so critical that she required extensive emergency medical care, multiple surgeries, and ultimately a life-saving leg amputation. Against all odds, Kallie never gave up. Today, Kallie is thriving on three legs, living the life she always deserved at Lions Tigers & Bears. She continues to receive specialized daily care from our dedicated team, and every step she takes is a reminder of what’s possible when compassion meets action. Your support made Kallie’s second chance possible. Thank you for standing with us as we rescue, rehabilitate, and provide lifelong sanctuary to animals who have nowhere else to turn. Happy International Tiger Day.
